test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct to Indirect Speech.

The captain said, "Stand at ease!"

options.text: The captain said to stand at ease.
The captain said that they should stand at ease.
The captain advised them to stand at ease.
The captain ordered them to stand at ease.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The captain ordered them to stand at ease.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"Stand at ease!" becomes "ordered them to stand at ease."**
 
 
• Reporting verb "said" changes to "ordered" to reflect the imperative tone of the command.
 
• The imperative verb "Stand" is converted to "to stand" in indirect speech.
 
• Second-person pronoun is omitted as the sentence is generalized.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• In indirect speech, no quotation marks are used.
 
• The reporting verb is followed by the object (if applicable) and the converted command.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The captain ordered them to stand at ease.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The captain said to stand at ease."

 
 
• Fails to capture the commanding tone of the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "The captain said that they should stand at ease."
 
 
• "Should" weakens the directness of the original imperative command.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The captain advised them to stand at ease."
 
 
• "Advised" is inappropriate, as the original speech is a command, not advice.
